PC: Hikers complete ALS initial assessment, primary and secondary assessment.
Another team member obtains vitals, history, and performs initial assessment of the patient
One team member immediately puts on PPE and then applies direct pressure to the wound using gauze

Evaluate for debris/contamination and remove as necessary. Assess upper extremity pulses/circulation. Assess neurologic status. Apply direct pressure to wound and hold for 10-15 minutes (simulated), apply tourniquet 5-10 cm proximal to wound if bleeding is not controlled.
Hikers continue to assess vitals and monitor bleeding control. Administer rehydration via a water bottle from their pack, and give extra layers if she is still cold.
MK: Recognize shivering, pallor, decreased capillary refill, dizziness with standing as signs of volume depletion via blood loss.
SBP: Assess and constantly reassess the scene for safety
Activate EMS as soon as cell service is available
Assess both the scene and the status of the patient to determine the safest manner of evacuating
Assess and execute the best manner of EMS activation
Give comprehensive patient sign-out to EMS
ICS: Approach patient in non-threatening way using appropriate communication
Keep patient updated with medical management in a level of detail appropriate to their level of understanding
Obtain consent to treat and proceed when possible
Assign clear team roles and responsibilities
Communicate effectively as a team, including using directed, closed-loop communication
